caps: 88 cap: production/analytics evidence is not connected to the complete visitor journey.
90 cap: journey proof must include real deployed runtime evidence and observability, not only local screenshots.
94 cap: accessibility and performance evidence must be attached for the real runtime.
100 cap: requires exceptional proven outcomes: benchmarked visitor journey, fresh production evidence, measurable contact/project engagement, stable CI, and polished bilingual UX.
Anti-goal cap: extra docs, tool inventory, fixtures, or internal workflow volume cannot raise the score unless connected to the visitor/operator outcome.

Feature depth: Les contrats et cas d'erreur des surfaces API devraient etre valides par des tests d'integration lisibles.
The portfolio should expose a proof-backed selected-work path where each project answers role, problem, constraints, shipped outcome, stack, and verification artifact in one scan.
The practical AI workflow signal should remain supporting evidence; do not turn it into the primary product unless analytics show visitors engage with it before contacting.
The contact journey needs an explicit success/failure state or measurable event, not only outbound links, because the business outcome is contact intent.
If there is an API route, its user-visible reason should be clear and tested; otherwise keep the portfolio static and remove backend ambiguity from the product story.
QoL: Reduce operator friction by making one command produce the production-like journey proof, screenshots, accessibility scan, link check, and event trace in a single dated artifact.
Make stale proof obvious: every visual/proof artifact should state target URL, commit, viewport, language, command, and timestamp.
Keep generated Autogrowth/runtime artifacts out of the visitor narrative; the operator needs them, but the visitor needs proof and contact clarity fast.
Automate the decision packet for future agents so they do not reread 155 markdown files to discover the same 88 cap.
UI/UX: Aucun signal accessibilite explicite; verifier clavier, focus, labels, contrastes et etats d'erreur.
The first viewport remains the highest-leverage surface: name, role, offer, proof strip, selected work CTA, contact CTA, and language switch must be visible without overlap on mobile and desktop.
The benchmark bar is dark, tactile, and human; any dashboard-like or agentic-control visual direction should be resisted unless it makes the work easier to evaluate.
Project cards should be inspectable, not decorative: visible artifacts, outcomes, and proof links matter more than visual density.
The next UI proof should include keyboard focus, contrast, mobile French copy length, no horizontal overflow, and image/anchor integrity on the deployed URL.

one_move: Run a production visitor-journey proof slice: land on the deployed URL, inspect selected work, switch language, trigger contact intent, capture desktop/mobile EN/FR screenshots, verify links/images, record a11y/performance summary, and attach any journey event evidence. This is the shortest path from 88 to the 90 band because it attacks the active cap instead of adding inventory.
score_roadmap: - 0-49 : define target, owner, runtime, verification, and the first real journey.
- 50-74 : make the project dependable: complete core flows, tests, errors, docs, and status.
- 75-89 : make it feel good: polish UX/QoL, reduce steps, automate proof, and expose outcomes.
- 90-99 : make it exceptional: benchmark, harden, measure, remove friction, and prove edge cases.
- 100 : maintain magnum opus evidence; freshness and restraint matter more than more features.
- Current band directive for fullstack : polish the core experience, remove friction, automate verification, and harden release paths.
autonomy_roadmap: - Current Autogrowth maturity reference : 890/1000 means the local runtime is robust, but field integration and long-run autonomy still gate 930+.

- 930+ axis 1, authenticated field connectors : move beyond CLI/export/local collection toward real GitHub, CI provider, Sentry, PostHog/analytics, Playwright Cloud, and production-log APIs with explicit auth status and access issues.
- 930+ axis 2, deeper modularity : keep shrinking the monolith by extracting deep checks, dashboard, scoring, rendering, state, policy, telemetry, and loop runtime behind testable module contracts.
- 930+ axis 3, blocking multi-agent orchestration : turn scout/builder/critic/judge into a quorum workflow with votes, vetoes, replayable rationale, memory, and explicit rejection reasons.
- 930+ axis 4, long-run loops : add schedules, budgets, multi-run stop conditions, crash resume, task queue, and decision history so improvement can continue safely across sessions.
- 930+ axis 5, cockpit-grade dashboard : add filters, diff viewer, score trend, run replay, risk map, attached proof, and field-signal drilldown.
- Project application : for `fullstack`, do not claim 930+ unless the evaluation proves terrain data, autonomous loop safety, and user/operator outcome evidence, not only static repo quality.

blocker_escape_lanes: If production analytics access is blocked, create a local event-trace artifact from the same instrumentation and record the missing auth/access as the blocker.

If contact telemetry cannot be captured, prove link integrity and add UTM or event-wrapper instrumentation in a separate low-risk slice.
If the obvious goal stalls, upgrade one selected-work proof card and validate bilingual content contracts; this creates visitor evidence without weakening the production gate.
